headline: POLARX HITS 24.8M OF 9.8% COPPER AT CARIBOU DOME — NORTHERN STAR JV EXTENDS SYSTEM 170M DEEPER
snippet: PolarX (ASX: PXX) delivered its best-ever drill results at the Alaska Range's Caribou Dome, with hole CD26-007 returning 24.8m at 9.8% Cu and 14.5 g/t Ag from just 2.4m depth including sub-intervals above 13% copper, and CD26-004 adding 22.6m at 8.1% Cu from 3.7m. Deeper step-out drilling extended known mineralisation approximately 170m vertically beneath the previous limit; the existing resource stands at 7.2Mt at 3.1% Cu. Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) is fully funding the 2026 program, having contributed US$6M for a 30% JV interest — with 1,700m of drilling still to come this season.

headline: COPPER NEARS ALL-TIME RECORD AT $14,737/T — STRAIT OF HORMUZ CLOSURE AND CHINA ACID BAN THREATEN 15% OF WORLD SX-EW OUTPUT
snippet: Three-month LME copper hit $14,737 per tonne — its second-highest close on record — as two converging shocks strip roughly a quarter of global sulfuric acid supply needed for SX-EW leach operations: Strait of Hormuz vessel suspensions (cutting Middle East sulfur shipments) and China's emergency halt on sulfuric acid exports. Chilean and DRC operations producing a combined ~2.7 million tonnes of SX-EW copper are down to 30–60 days of acid inventory, underpinning the International Copper Study Group's first structural 150,000-tonne deficit forecast since 2009. Southern Copper and Freeport-McMoRan jumped 4.9% and 5.4% respectively on the session.

headline: GOLD FALLS TO $4,340 DESPITE IRAN TANKER STRIKES — THE COUNTERINTUITIVE REASON MOST INVESTORS HAVE BACKWARDS
snippet: The US destroyed five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman overnight, sending Brent crude toward $100 — but gold dropped to a one-week low near $4,340 before recovering to $4,378. GoldSilver.com's analysis argues the move isn't a safe-haven failure: the oil spike feeds directly into inflation expectations, boosting the probability of a September 16 Fed rate hike to roughly 70%, and that yield-and-dollar headwind overwhelms any geopolitical safe-haven bid. Gold's real test comes Thursday (PPI) and Friday (CPI), not the military headlines.

headline: OIL HITS $100 AS US STRIKES FIVE IRANIAN TANKERS — MINING INPUT COSTS AND SHIPPING ROUTES UNDER ACUTE PRESSURE
snippet: Brent crude breached $100 per barrel after the US Navy destroyed five IRGC-linked oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday night, escalating the US–Iran conflict and prolonging suspension of commercial vessel flows through the world's most critical energy chokepoint. For miners, the shock creates a double squeeze: diesel accounts for 15–20% of open-pit operating costs, and acid supply for SX-EW copper leaching is now critically constrained. Analysts warn Brent could reach $120 if Hormuz traffic remains disrupted.

headline: ALBEMARLE TAPS BHP'S RAGNAR UDD AS NEXT CEO — WORLD'S LARGEST LITHIUM PRODUCER BETS ON MINING HEAVYWEIGHT
snippet: Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) named BHP Chief Commercial Officer Ragnar Udd as president and CEO effective February 1, 2027, with current CEO Kent Masters moving to executive chairman. Udd brings 25+ years running resources businesses across Australia, Asia and the Americas — a footprint that mirrors Albemarle's — and inherits what analysts describe as a '$250 million swing per dollar of lithium price' at the company's Chilean and Australian operations. The appointment signals Albemarle is shifting toward operational discipline over growth as surging energy-storage demand tightens the battery-metal market.

headline: PANORO DRILLS 808M OF COPPER-GOLD TO 1,100M DEPTH AT COTABAMBAS — PERU PORPHYRY OPEN IN FOUR DIRECTIONS
snippet: Panoro Minerals (TSXV: PML) reported hole CB-230 intersected 808m of hypogene copper-gold-silver mineralization from 296m to 1,104m depth, including a 156.5m interval at 0.38% Cu and 0.22 g/t Au and a 48.1m highlight at 0.57% Cu, 0.25 g/t Au and 4.08 g/t Ag within the Principal Porphyry. The results confirm high-grade continuity across ~600m of strike and extend the Cotabambas system to 1,100m below surface — with the deposit open to the north, south, southwest and at depth — a scale of porphyry geometry that underlies world-class deposits.

headline: URANIUM SPOT HITS $90/LB AS KAZATOMPROM ACID PLANT DELAYS BITE — JEFFERIES NAMES NEXGEN, CAMECO, BWX AS TOP NUCLEAR PICKS
snippet: Uranium spot approached the psychologically significant $90/lb mark as Kazatomprom revealed delays at its TQZ sulfuric acid plant, the input needed for in-situ uranium leaching, reducing 2026 output guidance to 27,500–29,000 tU. Jefferies issued a fresh sector note naming NexGen Energy (TSX/NYSE: NXE), Cameco (TSX/NYSE: CCJ) and BWX Technologies as top nuclear buys for September, with long-term contract prices at $90/lb — their highest since 2008. Long-term contracts at utilities are front-running what analysts call the next structural contracting cycle.

headline: SILVER'S UNSUNG STRENGTH: AVERAGED $74 IN 2026 — 117% ABOVE 2025 LEVELS — AND WHY THE PULLBACK ISN'T THE END
snippet: GoldSeek analysis notes silver averaged nearly $74 per ounce in 2026 year-to-date into early September — 116.7% higher than the comparable 2025 period — even after the first-half selloff. The piece argues that silver's relative resilience versus gold (trading near 12-year highs despite the pullback) reflects structural industrial demand drivers that haven't changed, while warning that vertical moonshots create high-risk entry points and that disciplined investors should wait for confirmation of the next leg rather than chasing the recent bounce.

headline: RARE EARTH MARKET SEPTEMBER 2026: CHINA'S EXPORT CONTROL SUSPENSION EXPIRES NOV 10 — THE BIGGEST SINGLE CATALYST ON THE CALENDAR
snippet: September's rare earth basket posted a near-flat month (+0.31% average, +0.22% median), with the NdPr magnet complex falling together as a unit for the first time since May. The market's dominant near-term catalyst is now clearly visible: China's suspension of its October 2025 export control escalation expires November 10, 2026 — roughly two months out — while the core April 2025 licensing regime on seven rare earth categories remains fully enforced. Investors positioned in Western producers including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth are watching whether Beijing renews, expands, or allows the suspension to lapse.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS HITS 27.0M AT 20.38 G/T GOLD AT ANTINO WEST — STEP-OUT OPENS NEW ZONE 1.2KM FROM FROYO
snippet: Founders Metals (TSXV: FDR) reported one of the best single intercepts in Antino's history from the first step-out drilling at the Upper Antino-West Zone in southeastern Suriname: hole FR251 returned 27.0m at 20.38 g/t Au from 100m depth, including 10.0m at 43.26 g/t Au. The West Zone sits 1.2km west of the established Froyo Zone — first hit by discovery hole FR217 (53.1m at 1.21 g/t from surface) — and is open along strike with five follow-up holes and drilling ongoing, flagging a potential lateral district expansion for this already high-grade Suriname gold project.
